analyzed_vuln.description: In htmlParsePI, the start check uses `if ((RAW == '<') && (NXT(1) == '?'))` without first ensuring enough buffered input for `NXT(1)`. When the parser is at end-of-input (or only one byte remains), `NXT(1)` reads past the input buffer, causing a 1-byte global-buffer-overflow read. The crash is reported at HTMLparser.c:3354 in this condition check.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The html fuzz harness calls `htmlReadMemory` with attacker-controlled bytes and options. During `htmlParseDocument`, loops repeatedly test for `<?` and call `htmlParsePI`. A malformed/truncated document that drives the parser to a boundary where `CUR` can be read but `NXT(1)` is out of range triggers the OOB read in `htmlParsePI` before any further validation. No special option is strictly required beyond reaching this parser state with crafted HTML/PI-like input.
